sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते । प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
hindiTranslation: हे पार्थ  परमात्माके सत्इस नामका सत्तामात्रमें और श्रेष्ठ भावमें प्रयोग किया जाता है तथा प्रशंसनीय कर्मके साथ सत् शब्द जोड़ा जाता है ॥
englishTranslation: O Partha, the word sat is used for existence itself, for noble being, and for praiseworthy action.
essence: What is real and worthy carries the mark of sat.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: The word sat is used for what truly exists, for noble character, and for good action.
simpleInsight: It gives a clean standard: what is real, noble, and worthy of praise deserves your full trust.
detailedMeaning: Krishna answers Arjuna, for whom every action now feels morally loaded. After saying that sacred acts should be offered without craving reward, he now explains the word sat: it points to reality, goodness, and worthy action.
modernRelevance: You sign a document you know is honest, even though no one is watching. The quiet relief comes from knowing the act itself is clean, whether or not it brings applause.
translationLiteral: सत् (sat; the real / the good) / भावे (in existence / being) / साधुभावे (in noble being) / च (and) / सत् (sat) / इति (thus) / एतत् (this) / प्रयुज्यते (is used) / प्रशस्ते (praiseworthy) / कर्मणि (in action) / तथा (also) / सत्-शब्दः (the word sat) / पार्थ (O Partha) / युज्यते (is joined / applied)
insight: Krishna explains sat: the word covers what exists, what is good, and any action worth praise.
